text:
ashley: Quick thread — proposal: implement "partial-redact-by-confidence" for request/response logs so we only fully redact when model/heuristic confidence > 0.9, and otherwise keep deterministic pseudonymization. Trying to reduce over-redaction and improve signal for debugging.

devon: +1 to reducing over-redaction. Can you sketch how this interacts with sampling quotas? we need to avoid accidental PII leakage in low-sample buckets.

ashley: thinking quota-aware flow: compute confidence -> if >= 0.9 mask with full redaction token `<REDACTED>` -> if 0.5-0.9 pseudonymize with stable hash -> if <0.5 keep as-is but mark as sensitive in metadata and send only to sampled telemetry streams. Also add TTL on unhashed values in the dev-only inspect store.

priya: curious about telemetry impact — we need dashboard metrics that show the distribution of confidence buckets, estimated cost delta, and % of routes affected. otherwise PMs will ask for numbers. can we add an estimated "redaction rate" metric per route?

jonathan: yes — console should show per-route: sample_rate, redaction_rate, pseudonymize_rate, and projected token-cost savings. UX note: a togglable heatmap for last 24h would be helpful.

sre-eli: security note: any time we keep unhashed values (even transiently) we must gate behind auditor-approval and KMS-encrypted storage. propose adding an "auditor-token" flow: request in console -> two approvers -> temporary 1h access. ops-bot: "Request received: audit-request-#1123" <@ops-bot>.

ashley: agree on approvals. Also proposing an explicit route-level override `force_full_redact` for regulated customers so their traffic never leaves redacted form regardless of confidence.

devon: implementation detail: where does confidence get computed? client-side model or our inference pipeline? if client, we trust them less. I prefer server-side using the same PII-detector model we run for embeddings. that'll keep behaviour consistent.

ashley: plan: run server-side detector in pre-processor (fast quantized model), emit `pii_confidence` field, then routing rules evaluate it. sample config (prototype):

```
{
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "redaction_policy": {
    "confidence_thresholds": {"full": 0.9, "pseudo": 0.5},
    "pseudo_hash_salt_id": "tenant-stable-v1",
    "force_full_redact": false,
    "inspect_flow": {"sample_rate": 0.01, "ttl_hours": 1}
  }
}
```

priya: small ask: console should compute estimated downstream reduction in tracing volume if we flip from current policy to this one. we can approximate using historical detector outputs. add a button "Estimate savings" in rollout modal.

jonathan: rollout strategy: canary 5% of routes for 48h, backfill metrics, then 25% for 24h, then 100%. add an automatic rollback if fraud/leak detection metric increases or if redaction_rate drops below expected threshold.

sre-eli: add an ops alert when any route's `unredacted_sampled_count` > 0 unexpectedly. also ensure retention policy for pseudonymized values matches compliance (e.g., scrub after 30d unless flagged).

ashley: good. question for infra — can we make pseudonymization deterministic across tenants but rotate salt per tenant monthly? devon?

devon: yes — keep salt per-tenant in KMS, rotate monthly, but persist a mapping for prior-salt hashes for 30d to allow debug correlation. rotation implementation will require a background migration job for any timeline depends on hash equality; otherwise we accept a small window of losing correlation.

priya: UX: in Console rollout modal show two toggles: "Enable partial redact" and "Enforce tenant override" + a readout of projected token cost change. include link to docs: https://intra.redwood/ops/redaction-partial

ashley: I'll open a proto PR with the detector hook + policy evaluator and a small dashboard mock. thanks team. :seedling:

ops-bot: "canary-deploy: started canary for route /v1/generate (5%) — id canary-17945"

jonathan: acknowledged, keeping an eye on telemetry. if anyone sees a spike in the "unredacted_sampled_count" ping #eng-oncall immediately.
